## [0.35.2] - 2026-09-22

A patch release. The one to update for: a data-driven single send could go
out with a template token still in it instead of the row's value. Also here:
a double-click on Get Token that could throw away the OAuth token it had just
fetched, two Settings buttons that widened while they worked, and a caret
shorter than its neighbors.

### Changed

- Re-sending a request now sweeps a faint band across the dimmed response
  pane while the new one is on its way, instead of a plain, motionless dim -
  the previous response underneath stays just as readable.

### Fixed

- **A single send with a bound data row could send a request with the wrong
  value - or none at all.** The row picker beside Send, and a single
  request's own load test, only filled in a token spelled `{{data.column}}`;
  a column referenced the plain way, `{{column}}`, reached the server exactly
  as written instead of that row's value. A collection run was never
  affected. If a request or its auth used the bare spelling, re-check what it
  actually sent before this fix - it was accepted by the server as literal
  template text rather than refused.
- **A second click after fetching an OAuth token could delete it.** Clear sat
  to the right of Get Token, and a token landing slid the button left by
  Clear's width - a normal double-click on the same spot hit Clear instead
  and threw away the token that had just arrived. The buttons no longer move
  once a token lands.
- In Settings, the Connection test card's Test button and the Add certificate
  button both widened while their request was in flight, shrinking the URL
  field beside Test and sliding Cancel sideways. Both now hold their size and
  swap an icon in place instead.
- The form-data row's text/file switch now crossfades between its two icons
  instead of swapping them in a hard cut under the pointer that just clicked
  it.
- The launcher and first-run screens now fade in like every other screen in
  that spot, instead of popping in with a hard cut.
- The row-picker caret between Send and Load Test - shown once a collection's
  CSV or JSON data file is bound - was a few pixels shorter than the buttons
  on either side of it.
